explanation: Repeatedly merge the two least frequent subtrees. Each merge increases the weighted code length by their combined frequency, so summing merge weights gives the total. Divide by 100 as this question’s contract requires; one symbol needs zero bits.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) time. Each of n−1 merges performs a constant number of O(log(n+1)) heap operations.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. At most n weights are live in the heap.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The two least frequent subtrees can be deepest siblings in an optimal prefix code. Merging them reduces the problem while increasing total weighted depth by exactly their combined weight. Repeating the greedy merge and summing merge weights therefore gives the optimal weighted length. The final division by 100 is the explicit corpus convention.
walkthrough: For frequencies R=12, S=18 and T=30, merge 12+18=30, then 30+30=60. The total weighted code length is 30+60=90, so return 90/100=0.9.
edgeCases: A singleton symbol can use an empty codeword and has result zero.
Equal weights may produce different optimal trees with the same weighted length.
Divide by 100 even if the supplied frequencies sum to a value other than 100.
